target.title: fix(discord): gate replyTo on first chunk for implicit-first replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With `channels.discord.replyToMode: "first"`, chunked replies send the native
Discord reply reference on ALL physical chunks, not just the first.  The
replied-to person gets N reply notifications for one logical answer.

Closes #99068

## Root Cause / Fix

In `sendDiscordText`, the `sendChunk` closure captures `replyTo` and passes it
unconditionally to every chunk body.  The `isFirst` flag controls components
and embeds but never gates `replyTo`.

Fix: add `suppressTrailingReply` flag (default `false` = backward compatible).
When `true`, gate `replyTo` on the first chunk only.  The flag is plumbed
through `sendDiscordText`, `sendDiscordMedia`, and `sendMessageDiscord` opts.

This preserves `replyTo` on all chunks for explicit reply tags and `"all"`
mode, while suppressing trailing chunks only for implicit single-use
(`"first"`) replies — matching ClawSweeper's guidance.

Also fix `sendDiscordMedia` trailing-chunk loop to pass `undefined` instead
of the inherited `replyTo`.

## Evidence

### Before (main — bug)

```
it("preserves reply reference across all text chunks")
  → ALL chunks get message_reference (bug for first mode)
```

### After (fix)

```
it("gates implicit-first reply to first text chunk only (#99068)")
  → first chunk: reply ✅  trailing chunk: undefined ✅

it("gates implicit-first reply to media caption chunk only (#99068)")
  → media caption: reply ✅  trailing text: undefined ✅

it("preserves reply across all text chunks for explicit/all mode")
  → all chunks: reply ✅

it("always suppresses reply on media trailing text chunks")
  → media caption: reply ✅  trailing: undefined ✅
```

### Test runner

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts
  Tests  46 passed (46)
```

### Pre-submit

```
oxfmt --check  ✓
oxlint         ✓
git diff --check ✓
```

## Change Type
- [x] Bug fix

## Scope
- [x] Discord channel (send layer)

## Security Impact
- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No
